chemistry-killer-06.goal: Analyze the underlying scientific principles and deduce the correct conclusion.
chemistry-killer-06.material:
The colour-change ranges of indicators are:
Methyl orange: red at pH < 3.1, orange at 3.1 to 4.4, yellow at pH > 4.4
BTB: yellow at pH < 6.0, green at 6.0 to 7.6, blue at pH > 7.6
Phenolphthalein: colourless at pH < 8.3, pink at 8.3 to 10.0, red at pH > 10.0
Three everyday aqueous solutions were tested with all three indicators.
(A) Stomach-acid model solution: methyl orange red, BTB yellow, phenolphthalein colourless
(B) Solution after an antacid was added and fully reacted: methyl orange yellow, BTB yellow, phenolphthalein colourless
(C) Dilute sodium hydrogencarbonate solution: methyl orange yellow, BTB blue, phenolphthalein colourless
If the pH range satisfying all three indicator results is narrowed down as far as possible, which option correctly gives the pH ranges of (A), (B), (C) in order?

chemistry-killer-06.s.s1.explain:

If the pH range satisfying all three indicator results is narrowed down as far as possible, which option correctly gives the pH ranges of (A), (B), (C) in order?
chemistry-killer-06.steps.0.explain:
(A): methyl orange red pH < 3.1, BTB yellow pH < 6.0, phenolphthalein colourless pH < 8.3. Common range: pH < 3.1.
(B): methyl orange yellow pH > 4.4, BTB yellow pH < 6.0, phenolphthalein colourless pH < 8.3. Common range: 4.4 < pH < 6.0.
(C): methyl orange yellow pH > 4.4, BTB blue pH > 7.6, phenolphthalein colourless pH < 8.3. Common range: 7.6 < pH < 8.3.
Answer: (A) pH < 3.1, (B) 4.4 < pH < 6.0, (C) 7.6 < pH < 8.3 (b). (Wrong options: reading (A) as 3.1 to 4.4 confuses red with orange; reading (B) as 6.0 to 7.6 confuses BTB yellow with green; the last option uses only the BTB range and is not the narrowest.)
